clue.text: African woman entertains people from Copenhagen, maybe

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them within, so the woman's name wraps round the people

parts.note: Sue is a woman's name
Copenhagen is the Danish capital, so its people are Danes; 'maybe' marks them as an example

explanation.surface: A woman from Africa hosts some visitors from Denmark's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Sudan, a country in Africa, is an African of that nation.

clue.text: Northerner offers small place to sleep

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Someone from the north offers a guest a little bed for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland lies in the north of Britain, so a Scot is a Northerner from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Park keeper with yen to stand behind old conservatory

indicators.note: the keeper and the yen are told to come after the old letter, so they follow it

parts.note: a ranger looks after a park or forest
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A park warden, with some Japanese money, stands behind an old glasshouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass-walled building for growing citrus trees, a kind of conservatory found in grand houses.

clue.text: Name of girl featured in American newspaper

indicators.note: a girl's name featured in a phrase is contained in its letters, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A girl's name appears in an American paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, as in the queen or the Brontë sister.

clue.text: Fondness shown by that cat moving deviously round people

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the people, holding them inside
letters moving in a devious, winding way end up rearranged

parts.note: men is a common crossword stand-in for people

explanation.surface: An affectionate cat sneaks slyly around some people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fondness shown' reads as one phrase, but 'shown by' is only a link; 'moving deviously' signals the anagram and 'round' the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an emotional bond to someone or something is a synonym for fondness.

clue.text: Outlaw, that is youth wearing sweatshirt

parts.note: Robin Hood is the famous outlaw, so Hood stands for outlaw
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: An outlaw, in other words, is a young person in a sweatshirt.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the word also names a young person in a hooded top, often with a hint of menace.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the name for a hooded top transferred to the youth who wears one.

clue.text: Ripon's dilapidated jail

indicators.note: a dilapidated building is falling apart, so its letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: The jail in Ripon, a cathedral city in Yorkshire, has fallen into disrepair.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name a building where offenders are locked up.

clue.text: Like the rich enjoying good health, cured so to speak

parts.note: someone in good health is well

indicators.note: signals that the word for cured is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: healed means cured

explanation.surface: Wealthy people stay healthy, perhaps because they can pay to be made better.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for wealthy, from the idea of having good heels on one's shoes.

clue.text: Heavy metal's main singer?

definitions.meaning: a dense, soft grey metal, chemical symbol Pb
the principal vocalist in a group takes the ... part

explanation.surface: The front man of a heavy metal band.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a dense element, and the principal performer, as in the lead vocalist.

clue.text: Foolish type, one taken in by female trader

parts.note: a clot is British slang for a stupid person

indicators.note: the one is held within the female's word, placed inside it

parts.note: her is the female pronoun
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A silly person gets conned by a woman who sells things.
explanation.walkthrough: CLOT is a mild British insult for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes or sells clothes is a particular kind of trader.

clue.text: Odd parts of garden we cultivated

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions, first, third, fifth and seventh, are taken

explanation.surface: Some strange corners of the garden we have tended.
explanation.definitionFit: To cultivate plants is to raise them, so the past tense matches the past participle sense of raised.

clue.text: Fashionable folk disturbed resident

indicators.note: something disturbed is moved out of place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stylish people have bothered someone living locally.
explanation.definitionFit: A plural noun for people who follow the latest styles, matching fashionable folk.

clue.text: Wintry weather today, after first sign of spring

indicators.note: the word for today comes after the first letter
the opening letter of the word spring is taken

parts.note: now means at the present time, today

explanation.surface: Cold weather has arrived today, just after spring first showed itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling flakes of frozen water are the classic example of wintry weather.

clue.text: Dreary poet gets upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned over, so the poet's word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A dull poet becomes annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: both mean dull, colourless and lacking interest.

clue.text: Two members of King Arthur's court reportedly sleep well

indicators.note: signals that the words are spoken, so their sound matters, not their spelling

parts.words: Two members of King Arthur's court
parts.note: Arthur's court was made up of knights of the Round Table, so two of them are two knights

explanation.surface: A pair of Arthurian knights wish each other a restful night.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedtime farewell, said as a wish that someone will sleep well.

clue.text: Current way to set pupils

definitions.meaning: a flow of water, as in a brook
in British schools, putting pupils into ability groups, or one such group

explanation.surface: The modern method of sorting schoolchildren.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as an adjective meaning modern, but it is the noun for flowing water.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook is a water current, and a school ability group is also called by this name.

clue.text: Chat? The opposite

definitions.meaning: the reverse or contrary of a statement

explanation.surface: Is this chatting? No, quite the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to talk; as a noun it means the reverse of something.

clue.text: Posting messages: rather cute thing, not hard

parts.note: twee, a British word, means overly sweet or quaint

indicators.note: says the hard letter is left out of the word thing

parts.note: taken from the clue, then shortened
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Sending online messages: a somewhat sweet activity, but not difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: TWEE is British for affectedly cute.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending short posts on the social platform once called Twitter is posting messages.

clue.text: King not up for a dance

parts.note: Charles is the name of several English kings

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken from the clue, then turned round

explanation.surface: A monarch declines to take part in a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not up for' looks like 'unwilling', but 'up' turns NOT round.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively 1920s jazz-age dance named after the city in South Carolina.

clue.text: Get up but forget to wear stocking?

definitions.meaning: an informal British command to get out of bed
taken literally, without a stocking a bare limb would be on view

explanation.surface: Someone rises but forgets to put on their hosiery.
explanation.walkthrough: This British idiom, originally a naval wake-up call, means hurry and get out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom telling someone to get up, read literally as displaying a bare limb.

clue.text: Husband, for example, organised meals out

indicators.note: to organise is to put in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A husband arranges meals at restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband is one example of a perfect life partner.

clue.text: Reporter who counts the votes?

definitions.meaning: an official who counts ballots, especially in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A journalist who tallies up the election ballots.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: one who tells a story, and the official who counts votes.

clue.text: Dress, note, cut short

indicators.note: the word for the note loses its final letter, so it is shortened

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note in American usage

explanation.surface: A note about a dress that has been shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A very short skirt or frock is called by this abbreviated name.

clue.text: Queen on top of unusually big statue

indicators.note: in a down clue, the queen sits above the other letters

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth
OS is the abbreviation for outsize, a clothing term for an unusually large size

explanation.surface: The queen stands on top of a remarkably large statue.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a specific statue: the winged figure in Piccadilly Circus, London, popularly named after the god of love.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Piccadilly Circus statue is popularly known by the name of the Greek love god.
